Why this corner

  1. Shovel-ready and right-sized. The pilot takes about 4 of Lot 5's 8.3 acres and leaves Lot 3 next door untouched.
  2. Two road frontages. Separate main and emergency gates, with the 8-inch water and sewer mains already drawn in Innovation Way.
  3. Short utility run. About 1,300 ft along Innovation Way to the high-pressure gas line and fiber in Iron Springs Road.
  4. Rail stays free. The lots along the railroad keep their frontage for heavy industry, including a transformer plant.
  5. Known ground. Boring B-6 of the 2023 geotechnical study sits on the pad itself.
  6. Room to grow in place. Lot 3 takes two more blocks, about 30 MW in total, plus a substation reserve. Going to 50 MW needs part of Parcel G or a denser layout.

The pilot fits inside the 11 MW the park lists as available today; the build-out depends on the planned substation. Design-day draw uses PUE 1.24–1.41 from our Texas study and should come in lower in Cedar City's climate; to be re-run.

Ground conditions

  • Interlayered silt, lean clay and sand to 51.5 ft; no groundwater encountered.
  • The upper 3–10 ft is porous and moisture-sensitive: allow for over-excavation and 1–7 ft of structural fill under foundations, 12–24 in under slabs.
  • On-site soil can be reused as grading fill, with 15–20% shrinkage.
  • AGEC asks for a lot-specific study before design.

From the AGEC geotechnical study for Phase 1, September 22, 2023.
